Standard D&D shortbow; no special campaign properties. Non-archer characters who want a bow default to this.

Arena-trained use: when you hit a restrained target with the tridens you deal +1d6 piercing (the tines find gaps in posture that an upright opponent would close). Personal property or arena supply only — not in the fort armory.

The curve allows attacks past a raised shield: once per turn your attack with the sica ignores the +2 AC bonus from a non-tower shield (the blade arcs around it). Standard Roman shields still apply if the wielder is in testudo stance.

Superior edge retention: ignore your first failed weapon maintenance roll each session. Balanced for formal use as well as combat: can be offered as a gift to a Roman officer (DC 12 Persuasion where a standard gladius would require DC 15). Rufus makes one per session rest at Camp Level 3.

Same shield-bending property as standard heavy pilum. On hit: extra mass disrupts target footing — target has disadvantage on their next Dexterity saving throw until start of their next turn. 2d commission surcharge per pilum above standard heavy pilum cost.

Rufus bands your existing scutum with iron strips. HP 30 (up from 15). Absorbs first 3 slashing damage per attack (iron bands deflect glancing blade hits). Shield bash deals 1d8 bludgeoning (up from 1d6). 40d commission above base scutum price. 4 lb heavier.

Worn under any armour; adds 4 lb but does not change AC or armour category. When you take a critical hit: roll one fewer extra damage die (minimum 1 extra die still applies). Quilting absorbs concentrated force. Does not stack with similar damage-reduction effects.

While you have a creature grappled or are grappled: that creature has disadvantage on all escape attempts. The quillon point creates a credible deterrent against sudden movement that a standard pugio blade does not.

Draw any weapon on this belt as a free object interaction without consuming your normal free object interaction for the turn. Accommodates up to 3 weapons in purpose-built loops. Replaces standard cingulum militare. Built to measure: non-transferable fit.

Stomp attack deals 1d6 bludgeoning against a prone creature (up from 1d4). Advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to maintain footing or resist being knocked prone. Iron studs replace standard hobnails: same Stealth disadvantage on stone floors.

Hand-balanced by Rufus for a specific thrower: +1 to attack rolls with these specific axes only (not other franciscae). Retrievable after combat. The bonus is personal: another thrower does not benefit from the balance.

Restores 2d6+2 hit points as an action (drinking) or bonus action (administering to adjacent unconscious ally). Fort supply controlled by Valeria; vicus supply from traveling merchants. 4 available at campaign start. Camp Level 2 restocks to 12.

Advantage on all saving throws against poison for 1 hour; if currently poisoned immediately ends the poisoned condition. Fort stock controlled by medicus. Vicus has independent supply via Sigrun's trade contacts. DC 14 Constitution saves in Session 3 benefit directly.

On hit: target takes 1d4 fire damage at start of each turn until extinguished (action + DC 10 Dex check or rolling prone). Sealed clay vessel: if dropped (fumble or fall) DC 12 Dex save or breaks under you. Effective against thatch structures in Session 3.

Scatter to cover a 5-ft square (action). Any creature moving through at normal speed takes 1 piercing damage and speed halved until spike removed (DC 10 Medicine or 1 minute self). No effect on creatures already at half speed.

Germanic NPCs (Vercingetorix, Thusnelda, tribal warriors) treat initial attitude as one step warmer when worn visibly. Religion DC 13 passive identifies origin tribe. No mechanical effect on Romans. Once a NPC knows you their personal opinion supersedes it.

One use. Present to a Germanic NPC before a social check: DC of that check reduced by 3. Sigrun carves the correct rune for the intended people; a wrong rune has no effect and she will tell you if you describe who it is for.

Burn while making a Religion or Insight check related to Germanic beliefs or ritual: advantage on that check. One use per bundle. The smell is distinctive: Roman soldiers present make DC 12 Wisdom save or treat you as one step more suspicious for 10 minutes.

5 rations per purchase. In Germanic contexts counts as a proper food offering (not travel rations). Germanic NPCs who see you share this treat initial attitude as one step less suspicious. Standard caloric and ration mechanics otherwise.

When hook is set on a fixed surface: advantage on Athletics checks to climb; on a failed climb check you slip but catch rather than fall (no falling damage from this specific check). Rope is 50 ft hemp: supports up to 300 lb.

20 iron pitons and a hammer. Setting pitons as you climb: on a failed Athletics climb check you stop but do not fall (costs 5 ft of movement to arrest). Does not prevent environmental falls (collapse or being shoved).
Dexterity check to pick locks or disable mechanical traps; proficiency applies if you have it. Listed on the vicus manifest as woodworking tools. The fort armory does not carry them.

Required to craft antitoxins and identify plant compounds. Advantage on Medicine checks to identify plant-based poisons or detect food and drink adulteration. Session 3 forest has nightshade and henbane: identifiable and usable with this kit.

5d per rumour; maximum 3 per session. Each is a current-events clue from the DM's prepared session list. Information is accurate: Brennus repeats what he heard, not what he invented. Interpretation is yours.

4 hours. For the next session only: +1 to attack rolls with one specific weapon type you already have proficiency in (chosen at training). Does not stack; re-purchasing resets the weapon type. Requires a veteran NPC with relevant experience to be available.

Advantage on Survival checks in one terrain type for one day (forest, road, fort environs, or frontier river crossing). The guide knows the territory and its hazards. Will not enter hostile encounters. Does not know campaign secrets.

Attack +6 to hit; DC 14 Str save or target knocked prone on hit; aerial targets: a trained crew who observed the creature's flight for 1 full round may attack without disadvantage (1d10+4 piercing); cannot be repositioned during combat without 6 soldiers spending their full action; wall-mounted only

Authority: issued to optio rank only. When used to prod a Roman soldier within 5 ft back into position (bonus action), that soldier makes a DC 11 Wisdom save or must comply immediately; on a success they comply on their next turn. Carrying one without optio rank is a disciplinary offence; any sergeant or officer who sees it will ask directly.

Standard D&D shortsword. Class substitution weapon for Bard, Rogue, and Monk. Common among auxiliary troops and arena-trained fighters. No campaign-specific formation bonuses; does not benefit from the gladius Formation Bonus property.

Standard D&D mace. Used by field clerics and chaplain aides who need a weapon compatible with one hand occupied by a holy symbol. Not issued by the armory; purchased from the vicus smith or brought from home. No campaign-specific properties.

Standard D&D quarterstaff. Class substitution for Monk, Druid, and Cleric. A length of hardwood cut to fighting height and fire-hardened. Available from the vicus carpenter or cut from any woodland timber in 10 minutes. No campaign-specific properties.

Standard D&D handaxe. Class substitution for Monk. Available from the vicus or fort smith. Carry two as paired one-handed weapons. No campaign-specific properties; Germanic-pattern variants look identical mechanically.

Standard D&D longsword. Officers' weapon and heavy cavalry side-arm. No campaign-specific properties distinct from the spatha; use this entry for class substitution (Paladin, Eldritch Knight, Fighter). Mechanically identical to the spatha for game purposes.

Germanic and Caledonian long-spear used in dense formations. Appears in Chapter 3 forest ambush. Cannot be used in tight spaces (corridors under 10 ft wide): attacks in such spaces are made at disadvantage. Cannot be used in any Roman formation. Not issued; encountered on enemies.

Short straight stabbing sword of Sarmatian and Parthian heavy cavalry. Worn at the right hip alongside the kontos scabbard; drawn when the lance is spent and range collapses. A character proficient with the shortsword transfers that proficiency to the akinakes automatically (same grip and technique).

Standard D&D dart. Class substitution for Monk. A weighted throwing spike functionally similar to the plumbata at close range but lighter and without the plumbata's arc advantage. Characters carry up to 10 without encumbrance. Freely available from the vicus.

Standard D&D javelin. Generic class substitution for Cleric, Druid, and Paladin who need a simple thrown weapon. Mechanically identical to the light pilum but without campaign special properties. Freely available from the fort quartermaster without requisition.

Standard D&D hand crossbow. Class substitution for Bard and Rogue. Not standard legion issue; found in fort stores as personal-purchase equipment. Loading: bonus action to reload between shots. Light property: can be used in the off hand alongside a one-handed weapon.

Standard D&D longbow. Not standard Roman issue (composite bow preferred for cavalry; sling preferred for infantry). Available from Batavian or Germanic auxiliary archers. Class substitution option. Requires STR 11+ for full draw; characters with STR 10 or below have disadvantage on attack rolls.
